{"status": "answered", "answer": "The Order API v1 sunset was accelerated following an incident on 2025-10-02 where order-service latency caused v1 clients to retry timed-out requests. Because v1 lacks an idempotency mechanism, these retries generated duplicate orders (resulting in duplicate charges and shipments). The sunset was accelerated to eliminate the risk of recurring duplicate orders by forcing remaining clients to migrate to v2, which enforces mandatory Idempotency-Key headers. The sunset date is 2025-12-31, after which all v1 requests will be rejected.", "citations": ["PM-2025-021@v1", "SPEC-ORDER-API@v1"]}

ADR-011 specifically notes there are no exemptions for this call. {"status": "answered", "answer": "payment-service applies an 8-second client timeout to every PayNimbus call. This timeout directly aligns with the PayNimbus contract response guarantee of 8 seconds at p99 (meaning 99 out of 100 calls should receive a response within 8 seconds). Aligning the timeout to the contract guarantee ensures payment-service does not wait longer than a healthy response should take when PayNimbus is degraded, and ensures that any client timeout corresponds directly to a response outside what PayNimbus contractually promises.", "citations": ["SPEC-PAY-INT@v2", "CT-PAYN-2024@v1"]}
